I stopped believing in 9th grade after I began attending seminary courses. My brother showed me the inconsistencies in the Book of Abraham translation and that set me up to leave the religion entirely after I began examining all of its claims.

It was a gradual pile of questions over a decade (through missionary service, undergrad at BYU, and my first job). It resulted in my "doubling down" on church (callings, scriptures, meetings, dating) until I had a nervous breakdown at the YSA ward one day.

I went less active and realized my life was getting better, not worse. Made be finally look at my pile of questions objectively. I'm amazed how much of the faith I'm come to dismiss. I still appreciate the "good" parts of Mormonism (being nice, service, honesty), but they seem to be hardly unique.

My breakdown was about 12-18 months ago, and my "it clicks, I'm emotionally out now" moment was about 6 months ago.
Studying the new testament in seminary killed off any residual belief in Christianity that I was harboring, it wasn't just Mormonism I left behind.

I left after my mission, about 20 years ago. My testimony was cracked by the wackiness going on inside of the temple and the fact they had a cash register. I knew enough about Jesus to realize a cash register would not be found in his temple. The corporate nature of the religion was completely at odds with the church I experienced at the local level (I never paid attention at conferences). It has taken me decades to get over the ingrained fear and wacky ideas that are a part of growing up Mormon. I had my name removed a year ago and I feel that finally set me free.

Fairly recently.

I have used such automatic boxes and found 3 causes over the years.

First, clean the box, make sure the censors are not being blocked and causing it to continuing cleaning over and over again, which can confuse or even go off when the poor cat is trying to use it,

second, take all the cats to the vet, urinary tract infections cause cats to be weird about the litter box, one may have an infection that is causing the other to not use the box,

third, get a regular box and place them side by side. You may never get them to use it again, but right now you need to get them using any box again.

1) you never change litter suddenly. It freaks the cats out. You're supposed to do it gradually.

2) those automatic litter boxes that rotate are disgusting. Stop using them.

Your only best bet is to just put a standard box out there and put half of the old litter and half of some new stuff and mix it up. It would also help if you can save a poop sample from the cat's last accident and mix it up in the box, too. Smelling their own poop will help them know it's THEIR box.
I've been told over and over again to have one box per cat, in different locations. That's a good fallback method to try if nothing else is working.
